root_cause.text: In libceph's osdmap_decode(), the bounds validation for per-OSD osd_weight entries used a single sizeof(*map->osd_weight) instead of map->max_osd times that size, so a corrupted max_osd could make the decode loop read past the end of the incoming osdmap buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit message state that osd_state and osd_weight are decoded “for each osd, i.e., map->max_osd times,” but the original ceph_decode_need() “only accounts for sizeof(*map->osd_weight) once”; the patch changes the check from `sizeof(*map->osd_weight)` to `map->max_osd*sizeof(*map->osd_weight)` in `net/ceph/osdmap.c`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the decode size check to require space for the full osd_weight array before parsing the OSD map.
intent_record.what: The size argument passed to ceph_decode_need() was changed from adding a single sizeof(*map->osd_weight) to adding map->max_osd * sizeof(*map->osd_weight), so the required decode buffer now accounts for an osd_weight element for each OSD entry instead of just one.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the decoder now validates that enough input data is available for the entire osd_weight array before decoding, preventing underestimation of the required buffer size when map->max_osd is greater than 1 and avoiding invalid or unsafe parsing of truncated input.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the faulty bounds validation in osdmap_decode() by checking for enough space for the entire osd_weight array (map->max_osd * element size), which is the stated root cause of the out-of-bounds read.
